title: Gathering Materials & Rarity
summary: Gathering materials are twelve stackable crafting resources whose only purpose is paying for cosmetics at the Crafting Altar. Nine drop from ordinary Hub play and three are exclusive to Diamond Trophy runs, but every player's held quantities are the same account-wide no matter which server they're on. Every material, along with every other bag item, cosmetic and altar recipe, is tagged with one of six rarity tiers that colors its name and tooltip the same way across the whole network.
how_it_works:
Materials live in the 'Materials' category of your Backpack, in either the 'gathering' sub-tab (the nine Hub materials) or the 'dt_gathering' sub-tab (the three Diamond Trophy materials). All twelve stack without any limit, so holding thousands of one never fills up your bag. 

There are three ways to earn them: opening pocket bags and crates is the main source, quest rewards are second, and a small passive trickle drops just from playing (a finished parkour run, an arena kill, the daily chest, and on Diamond Trophy a mob kill, an act clear, defeating the Goblin King, or - very rarely - smashing a pot). That passive trickle is capped per player per day network-wide so it stays a top-up rather than something worth grinding on its own.

The three Diamond Trophy materials (Goblin Skin, Cannon Ash, Orange Plastic) only ever drop inside Diamond Trophy, and the game will never let a hub-wide cosmetic recipe require one of them - recipes that use a Diamond-Trophy-only material are themselves restricted to Diamond Trophy, so no cosmetic anyone can wear anywhere forces a trip into that gamemode to finish.

The only thing materials are ever spent on is the Crafting Altar: a recipe lists a handful of materials (sometimes alongside coins, and sometimes gated behind a one-off 'blueprint' item you have to find first) and consumes them all at once to start a timed craft. When the timer finishes, collecting the job grants the cosmetic. One recipe is an exception and produces a Common Key instead of a cosmetic - a way to turn spare materials into an extra crate-opening key.

Every item on the network - materials included - carries a rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary or Mythic, lowest to highest, each with its own color that shows on the item's name and as a line in its tooltip. A recipe's rarity also sets how long it takes to craft when the recipe doesn't specify its own duration.

Separately from the twelve gathering materials, the Materials tab's 'crafting' sub-tab holds two more crafting resources: Stardust, a genuine higher-tier ingredient already required by some Legendary and Mythic recipes (the Golden Crown hat and the Angel Wings back cosmetic both need it), and the Cosmetic Shard, described in its own tooltip as being for crafting cosmetics and dropped by crates, pocket bags and the daily chest. As of the current build, no live altar recipe actually spends a Cosmetic Shard - internal planning notes describe an unbuilt 'shard shop' feature that would let a player buy cosmetics directly with them (and would add shard costs to some existing recipes), but that feature has not shipped.
how_to_access: Materials are never bought or requested with a command - they simply land in your bag as you play, open containers, and complete quests. To see what you're holding, open your Backpack with /bag (aliases /backpack, /inv) and go to the Materials category, or check the Crafting Altar's own 'Your Materials' screen, which the Backpack's Keys & Materials shortcut opens directly. To spend them, open the Crafting Altar itself - with /altar if you're MVIP rank or higher, or by interacting with the Crafting Altar furniture placed in the world, which any player can open regardless of rank.

guis.title: Crafting Altar
guis.description: The only place gathering materials are spent. Browse cosmetic recipes, see what you can currently afford, start a timed craft, and track your running jobs.
guis.how_to_open: /altar (MVIP+), or interact with the Crafting Altar furniture in the world (open to every rank)

slots.action: Opens the craft-slots screen: your running jobs, their countdowns, and any free or locked slots
Opens a flat grid of every material and how much of it you're holding
Click to open that recipe's detail screen, showing its ingredients, cost, rarity and craft time, and whether you can currently afford it
Cycles the recipe list between Everything and one cosmetic kind (hat, body, balloon, off-hand)

guis.notes: A recipe you can't yet make is shown greyed out rather than hidden, so the catalogue reads as a checklist of what's still ahead rather than a shorter list than you remember. A recipe locked behind a blueprint you don't own yet shows as a locked silhouette until you find that blueprint.

open_questions: Whether the planned 'shard shop' (spending Cosmetic Shards to buy cosmetics directly) has any ETA - internal notes describe it only as an unbuilt mechanic.
Whether Cosmetic Shard will be folded into an existing altar recipe's cost before the shard shop ships, since no live recipe currently consumes it.
